summary: This is a Makefile with two targets both named 'hello'. When you run 'make hello', only the second one executes because Makefile targets with duplicate names get overwritten — the second definition replaces the first. Each target uses @echo to print a message without showing the command itself.

explanations.2: The @ symbol tells make to execute the echo command silently, so you only see the output 'Hello world' without seeing the echo command printed first.
explanations.5: This second 'hello' target overwrites the first one with the same name, so running 'make hello' will only ever print 'Nice to meet you'.
